notes: Slate grey stucco flats with a dark charcoal base storey. North end: round curved bay from storey 1 up; single tall dark-framed sash windows and one wide picture window; dark bracketed cornice. Ground: glazed double entry door and a glazed grid garage door, dark planting bed; uphill part of the frontage is a plain wall behind the garden. Slate grey darkened and base charcoal deepened, one more window in the uphill run. Wall dark charcoal-slate, base near-black. Round bay is a glazed half cylinder (storeys 1-2) with plates as dark bands and its own cap. Windows are plain dark-framed openings without sills: the first upper storey has a wide picture window (left), one centre and one right window; the top storey has a single window centred on the flat wall. Dark cornice. A set-back roof block (penthouse) at the top left inside the LiDAR allowance. The data's storey count (3) is kept, so the extra real storey cannot be drawn. Window-frame pilasters thinned so they no longer cut through the dark base; wall pushed darker. Wall pushed to dark charcoal-slate and base near-black; frame seams flattened out of the stucco; round bay drawn with one large pane per facet. Wall a neutral medium slate grey (blue cast removed) over a darker charcoal ground storey, window seams reduced to the openings only; the corner round bay is a solid grey drum with punched dark-framed windows on its curved facets, starting above the three-window storey; the upper storey has one window centred over the middle window below; ground: recessed black-framed glazed entry at the left third and a black-framed multi-light glazed garage centre-right; the bracketed cornice is replaced by a thin dark plain cap. Storey count stays the data 3 (spec-locked), so the extra real storey is not drawn; the setback penthouse block stays. Rework B: the street shows 4 storeys (dark ground + 3 upper), so storeysSeen 4 (2.8 m ground, 2.5 m uppers) replaces the roll count; wall a cool charcoal slate at the luminance floor over a darker #2c2f35 charcoal base course; the round oriel spans the two top storeys with the wall colour, a flat window under it on storey 2; storey 2 keeps wide-left / centre / under-bay windows, storeys 3-4 only the centre window plus the oriel; a dark bracketed stepped cornice replaces the thin fascia. Not doable: one large window plus a narrow side light per oriel storey (kit draws a sash per facet), the recessed panel round the centre window, and removing the frame-grid column seams (the per-storey window pattern needs the grid). Ground entry and window frames pushed to near-black steel so the recessed entry reads as a black-framed glazed door beside the black gridded garage (the doorway itself stays an open walk-in passage; sidelights are not drawable on a narrow door span). Rework 2: the corner oriel is a smooth 7-facet glazed bow (one wide curved window band per storey in dark frames between solid plates) instead of a 5-facet bay with a sash per facet; flat-wall window frames white on the charcoal wall; the penthouse block moved 1 m back from the front so it shows over the cornice. Not doable: the cornice wrapping the bow, windows in the penthouse block, and a closed dark glazed entry door (kit doors stand open for walk-in; the lit lobby shows through).
